source_evidence: A subscription-based fee is a set, recurring fee that you pay for a particular service, typically on a monthly basis. An asset-based fee is calculated as a percentage of the assets in your account.
answer: Subscription-based and asset-based advisory fees are calculated differently. A subscription-based fee is a set recurring amount, often charged monthly. An asset-based fee is a percentage of the money in your account, so the dollar amount of the fee changes as your account’s value changes. For comparison, you can annualize a monthly subscription fee and compare it with your account balance: a $3 monthly fee costs $36 per year, which is more than 7% of a $500 account.
formula_latex: \text{Annual subscription fee} = \text{Monthly fee} \times 12;\quad \text{Effective fee percentage} = \frac{\text{Annual subscription fee}}{\text{Account balance}} \times 100\%
